topicName: Test Scenarios, Test Cases, and Traceability Matrix (RTM)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Tutorial: Test Scenarios, Test Cases, and Traceability Matrix (RTM) in Manual Testing"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"In manual software testing, bridging the gap between requirements and actual test execution is critical for ensuring quality. This tutorial explores the foundational concepts of Test Scenarios, Test Cases, and the Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM), explaining how they interconnect to guarantee comprehensive test coverage."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"1. Test Scenarios"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A test scenario is a high-level statement of what needs to be tested. It is derived from business requirements and user stories, representing a specific functionality or feature that can be tested from an end-user perspective."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Purpose: Determines "what" to test without going into granular step-by-step details."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Source: SRS (Software Requirement Specification), Use Cases, or Business Requirements Documents."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"Example Test Scenario for a Login Page:
- Verify the login functionality with valid credentials.
- Verify the login functionality with invalid credentials.
- Verify the behavior of the forgot password link."},{"order":8,"type":"heading","text":"2. Test Cases"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"A test case is a granular, step-by-step document designed to verify a specific aspect of a test scenario. It contains precise inputs, execution steps, preconditions, expected results, and post-conditions."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Test Case ID: A unique identifier (e.g., TC_Login_001)."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Test Steps: Actionable instructions the tester must follow."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Expected Result: The exact system behavior anticipated by the tester."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Actual Result: The real system behavior observed during execution."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"Sample Test Case Structure:
- Test Case ID: TC_LOGIN_01
- Description: Verify login with valid username and password.
- Pre-condition: User must be on the login page.
- Execution Steps: 1. Enter valid username. 2. Enter valid password. 3. Click Login button.
- Expected Result: User should be redirected to the dashboard page."},{"order":15,"type":"heading","text":"3. Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM)"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"The Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM) is a document that maps and traces user requirements with test cases. It ensures that all requirements defined in the SRS are covered by at least one test case, eliminating gaps in testing."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Benefits of RTM"},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Ensures 100% test coverage against software requirements."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Highlights any missing requirements or orphaned test cases."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Helps in impact analysis when requirement changes occur mid-project."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"Sample RTM Matrix Format:
[Req_ID] | [Requirement Description] | [Test Scenario ID] | [Test Case ID] | [Status]
REQ_001  | User login functionality     | TS_Login_01        | TC_LOGIN_01    | Passed
REQ_002  | Password encryption         | TS_Security_01     | TC_SEC_05      | Failed"},{"order":22,"type":"heading","text":"Summary"},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"Mastering test scenarios, test cases, and RTM is essential for manual testers. Scenarios provide breadth, test cases provide depth, and the RTM provides accountability and complete project visibility."}]
